headline: Bruins stay hot with comeback win against Sharks at the Garden
morning_brew: Saturday night at the Garden was an absolute heater that proved why you never walk out of a hockey game early. Watching the boys erase that third-period deficit with a flurry of goals reminded me exactly why I endure the stress of this sport, as James Hagens and David Pastrnak lit the lamp in rapid succession to turn the tide. That points streak is sitting at eight games now, and for a team that looked like it had no answers earlier this season, this group is starting to look like a legitimate juggernaut.

Jeremy Swayman didn't have his sharpest night between the pipes, but he held the line when the pressure ratcheted up, which is what you need from your starter. It was a hell of a battle against San Jose, but pulling out that victory while the offense spreads the scoring around is a massive deposit into the Duck Boat fund. I am trying my best to stay cool and not get ahead of myself, yet seeing the lineup clicking like this is making it awfully difficult to remain a cynical Boston fan.

Looking ahead, we have a few days to catch our breath before hitting the road to take on Carolina on Tuesday. I am hoping the rest of the city keeps this momentum rolling because we have some serious hockey to play before the calendar turns. My neighbor Rick is already busy plotting out his next dossier on the officiating crews, so I might just take a break from the noise and enjoy the fact that for once, the scoreboard is finally leaning our way.

trend_watch.trend: Pastrnak buried a clutch goal in the third period to ignite a late rally against San Jose.
trend_watch.dans_take: When Pasta finds the back of the net in a tight game, the whole building just feels like it's gonna take flight.

trend_watch.trend: Hagens found the back of the net during a critical stretch of the final period to break the tie.
trend_watch.dans_take: The kid has serious poise under pressure and that goal was smoother than a fresh cup from Dunks.

trend_watch.trend: Swayman turned aside twenty-three shots on goal to secure the win in front of the home crowd.
trend_watch.dans_take: He wasn't perfect, but he stood tall when it mattered most, which is all I can ask for.
